commit_note: RAISED 7 -> 8 by the measured census, never chosen: region_charge_gate reports 8 of 16 CHARGED once cortex/brain.py feeds the insula terminus its declared body_in frame. A floor may rise and may never fall, so this artifact is the ratchet and bumping it to 9 is the reachable red (verified at T039: the gate returns rc=1 with 'REGION CHARGE GATE RED: N charged < floor'). The integer alone was never the point -- see identity_gap.

identity_gap.why_this_block_exists: FR-015 pins the floor's IDENTITY, not only its integer. Recording a count without this block would let the count stand in for the thing it is about, which is the failure this gate was built to prevent -- and it nearly did: at T039 the integer read 7 only because two UNNAMED regions charged in place of two NAMED ones, so the identity was 5 of 6 while the count looked complete. CLOSED at T039f: named_and_NOT_charged is now empty and the identity is 6 of 6. What retired the gap was NOT the import that made insula reachable -- that import would have flipped the region on its own, with or without a consumer -- but the measurement that the consumer's own output changes (tests/test_interoceptive_ignition.py). The cheap half and the evidence half are recorded separately here on purpose.
